extracted.intended_audience: Authors submitting manuscripts to PLOS One (researchers in life, health, and earth sciences) who wish to post or transfer preprints
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for authors on using PLOS One's direct transfer and facilitated posting to bioRxiv/medRxiv/EarthArXiv, and on preparing preprint files, updates, screening, and concerns handling. Focused on the practical and policy requirements for preprint posting associated with PLOS One submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct transfer service availability
rubrics_metrics.description: PLOS partners with openRxiv to make posting preprints in the life and health sciences seamless and convenient. Authors posting preprints to the bioRxiv or medRxiv preprint servers can choose to concurrently submit their manuscripts to PLOS One or another relevant PLOS journal through the direct transfer service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the direct transfer if you want concurrent submission/posting; learn more via bioRxiv/medRxiv links provided by PLOS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facilitated preprint posting opt-in
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors submitting manuscripts in the life, health and earth sciences to PLOS One may opt-in to have PLOS forward their submission to bioRxiv, medRxiv or EarthArXiv, depending on the scope of the paper, for consideration for posting as a preprint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Opting in triggers forwarding; papers must pass an initial screening for suitability to be posted. If later accepted for publication, the preprint and published article will link to each other.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility and independence from editorial assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligibility to post on bioRxiv, medRxiv or EarthArXiv is independent from the editorial assessment and peer review process. Preprint checks do not impact the decision regarding suitability for publication in PLOS One.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not assume server screening results affect journal editorial decisions; PLOS editorial selection is separate (see PLOS One editorial selection guidance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Preprint file format requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Preprints appear on bioRxiv, medRxiv or EarthArXiv in PDF format. Authors can choose to supply their own preprint PDF or have PLOS One compile an automatically generated PDF.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you supply a preprint PDF it will appear on the preprint server unchanged. Alternatively, PLOS can auto-generate a PDF from your manuscript and figures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required content in supplied preprint PDF
rubrics_metrics.description: Be sure to include title, authors, abstract, and the full text of the manuscript, along with any figures or tables and their captions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the supplied PDF contains all manuscript components; missing elements could affect posting or reader comprehension.

rubrics_metrics.name: PDF file size limit and compression
rubrics_metrics.description: Each of these preprint servers limits PDF file size to 40 MB or less. PDF files must be compressed to meet this requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compress figures/images and check overall PDF size before submission. If using auto-generated PDFs, verify final file size and compress if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary information and auto-generated PDFs
rubrics_metrics.description: Supplementary information will not be included in auto-generated preprints, but may be uploaded directly to the preprint server after posting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If supplementary files are important for readers, upload them separately to the preprint server after posting or supply a preprint PDF that includes them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure quality and formatting recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: Note that some figure quality may be lost during the auto-conversion process. For best results, make sure that your submission materials meet journal formatting requirements, and that tables fit within the margins of the page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If concerned about figure resolution, consider supplying a preprint PDF alongside your other submission files. Ensure figures/tables follow journal formatting to reduce conversion issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preprint screening and posting timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: After authors have opted in to have their preprint posted by PLOS One, it is transferred to bioRxiv, medRxiv or EarthArXiv where researchers with relevant expertise screen preprint submissions for suitability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Most submissions that pass the servers’ preprint checks will be posted within a few days of submission. Authors will receive a notification of successful preprint posting directly from the preprint server; the server will also contact authors if issues arise or the manuscript is not eligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-posting permanence and removal policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Once posted, a preprint cannot be removed except in rare cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be sure you are comfortable with public posting because removal is generally not possible; consult the preprint server's policies for the narrow circumstances that allow removal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encouragement to update preprints and post peer review history
rubrics_metrics.description: To ensure that readers are always accessing the latest version of the manuscript, authors are encouraged to submit updates and revisions to the relevant preprint server directly. Authors have permission to post the peer review history of their manuscript alongside their preprint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upload revised versions as they become available; consider posting peer review history to signal that the preprint has been peer reviewed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of concerns linking preprints and published articles
rubrics_metrics.description: If a concern arises about a published PLOS article with a related preprint, PLOS will evaluate the concern according to our standard editorial processes, taking into account any relevant comments available on the preprint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments and discussions on the preprint may be considered during editorial investigations; authors should monitor and respond to substantive concerns raised on the preprint server.
